title: improv·artist · industrial (Donald Judd)
mutation_directive: improv artist: industrial via Donald Judd

improv_extras.practice: stacked metal boxes; precise repetition; specificity of object

v1.feedback: The Judd stack reads clearly — eight evenly spaced boxes with area-weighted particle distribution on each face, aluminum-gray lit surfaces, and amber-tinted bottom faces evoking his colored plexiglass interiors. The slow orbiting light is a smart choice that reveals the box geometry over time without adding noise. To push it further: the boxes currently feel a bit flat because particles only sit on surfaces — adding a thin interior shell or partial transparency on the top face so you can peer down into the amber cavity would better capture Judd's specificity-of-object ethos. The morph-from-grid intro animation is unnecessary heritage baggage; start formed and let the light do the revealing.

v2.feedback: Strong Judd translation — the stacked open boxes with amber interior bottoms and sparse top faces read immediately as his Marfa aluminum/plexiglass progressions. The breathing animation is appropriately restrained but could be even more minimal or removed entirely to honor Judd's insistence on stillness; the micro-vibration, while subtle, slightly undermines the 'specificity of object' mandate. Consider adding a very slow orbital camera drift (0.5°/s) so the viewer can perceive the interior volumes and amber glow from shifting angles — right now the fixed 32° FOV from front-center flattens the depth that makes Judd's work physical. The warm background and aluminum palette are well-chosen; the piece would benefit from slightly more particles on interior surfaces to strengthen the amber-through-opening moment that defines these sculptures.
